topic: Holiday gifts: $25 per client deduction limit; employee cash/gift cards are taxable wages; small non-cash holiday gifts can be de minimis (LinkedIn, seasonal)
label: Holiday season / Tip
headline: Holiday gifts: what the IRS *lets you deduct*

items.title: Gifts to clients: $25 each
items.text: Per person, per year. Shipping and engraving don't count toward it.

items.title: Gift cards to employees
items.text: Cash and gift cards are taxable wages. Run them through payroll.

items.title: A small non-cash gift
items.text: A fruit basket or a book can be a non-taxable de minimis gift.

items.title: Hosting a holiday party?
items.text: Keep receipts and the guest list with your books.

ig_caption:
Planning holiday gifts for clients or your team? A few IRS rules decide what you can deduct.

1. Gifts to clients and referral partners: you can deduct up to $25 per person per year. Incidental costs like engraving, packing and shipping don't count toward the $25.
2. Cash and gift cards to employees can never count as a "de minimis" benefit. They're taxable wages, so run them through payroll.
3. A small, occasional non-cash holiday gift to employees (think a fruit basket or a book) can be a non-taxable de minimis fringe benefit.
4. Keep the receipt plus a note of who received each gift and why. That's what holds up if the deduction is ever questioned.

A $200 bottle of wine for your best client is still a $25 deduction. Spend what you like, just budget the tax on the rest.

Sources: IRS Small Business FAQ (business gifts) and IRS de minimis fringe benefits guidance. General information, not tax advice.
